 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/ for the death of Prakash.A S/o Late Abayappa.G in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 25.06.2020 at about 3.00 p.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 Prakash.A was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing No.KA51EE6500 on Anekal Smt.Lakshmamma vs Danappa on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186881783/
2 main road, Bengaluru, at that time, one canter bearing Registration No.KA 51C 1286 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the Prakash.
Due to impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, said Prakash was shifted to Best Hospital, Bangalore and he was under coma and lost his breath on 08.08.2020.
Prior to the accident, said Prakash was hale and healthy and he was working as mason and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending on the income of the deceased.
The said accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of canter.
The Respondent No.1 is the driver, Respondent No.2 is the owner of the canter and the Respondent No.3 is the insurer of the said vehicle.
Therefore, all the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.2 remained absent.

Hence,
he was placed exparte.
Respondent No1 and 3 appeared before the Court through their Counsels and filed Objections to the main petition.

Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending canter.
Further, he has contended that the canter is insured with the Respondent No.3 and the policy is valid as on the date of the accident.
He was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

Respondent No.3 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending canter.
Further, it has admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the canter bearing No.KA51C 1286.

Further it has contended that the Respondent No.2 knowingly and willfully has handed over the possession of the vehicle to the driver of the canter who was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, Respondent No.3 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues.:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that they are the legal representative of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that Prakash.A S/o Abayappa.G died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 25.06.2020 at about 3.00 p.m. near Smt.Lakshmamma vs Danappa on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186881783/
3 Gowdas Bar turning, Mayasandra, Anekal main road, Attibele Hobli, Anekal Taluk,
Bengaluru, arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of canter bearing No.KA51C1286?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 20 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.20 and they also examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.P.21 to P.24 and closed their side evidence.

On the other hand, Respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4 and Respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.2 and got maked a document as per Ex.R.5 and closed his side evidence.

Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioners and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record and citations relied by the learned counsel for the Petitioners, my answer to the above Issues are as under:

4  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No. 4 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS  7. Issue No.2: It is the case of the Petitioners that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the canter bearing No.KA51C1286 and in the said accident, Prakash had sustained injuries and succumbed to the said injuries.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 and 3 have denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending canter.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and reiterated the petition averments.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.

Ex.P1 is the True copy of FIR along with complaint which shows that the Attibele Police have registered the case against the driver of canter for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the Spot panchanama along with sketch map.
Ex.P.3 is the IMV Report which shows that accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of Inquest Panchanama.
Ex.P.5 is the PM report which shows the cause of death is due to severe head injury.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of Intimation regarding MLC.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of Intimation regarding death.

Ex.P8 is the copy of the Chargesheet which shows that the I.O of Attibele Police station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending canter for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC.

The Column No.17 of charge sheet reads as under:

12.
PW.1 has examined one witness by name Rajappa.T as PW.2.
PW1 and 2 were subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.3.

But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the PW.1 and PW.2.
13.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1.
RW.1 has produced 4 documents as per Ex.R.1 to R.4.

is the Insurance policy.

In the cross examination, he has admitted that the offending vehicle had valid policy.
14. The Respondent No.1 got himself examined as RW.2 and got marked driving licence as per Ex.R.5.
He has admitted that his vehicle was seized and the owner has got released the vehicle.
Further, he admitted that he has not challenged the Charge sheet.

15. Though, the Respondent No.3 in his evidence had taken contention that the said accident has not been occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of canter and due to negligence of deceased and there is no cogent evidence is produced to prove the said fact.
Charge sheet is the material document which was submitted by the I.O after thorough investigation against the driver of the offending canter.

Hence, PW.1 has proved the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending canter and in the said accident, her husband Prakash had sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative".
16. Issue No. 1 and 3:
Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased and Petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased Prakash.

In order to prove this fact, PW.1 has produced her Aadhar Card and the Aadhar cards of the petitioner No. 2 and 3 and the deceased Prakash and Election ID card of the deceased and got marked it as Ex.P9 to 12.

Upon going Smt.Lakshmamma vs Danappa on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186881783/
6 through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased with the Petitioners.

sentences.text: Hence, the Petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Prakash.
17. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 48 years and his avocation is shown as mason and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
PW.1 has not produced any documents to prove the occupation of her deceased husband.
In the absence of any proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

As the said accident has been occurred in the year 2020, the notional income of the deceased to be taken at Rs.14,500/p.m.
18.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Prakash as 48 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.11 i.e., Aadhar card of the deceased Prakash, which shows the date of birth of Prakash as 02.05.1972.
The alleged accident was occurred on 25.06.2020.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Prakash was 48 years.
Hence, the age of the deceased Prakash to be taken at 48 years for the purpose of calculation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
20.
The deceased has left behind him, his wife and son and mother.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 14,500/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No. 2 is son and Petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased Prakash, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 40,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 15,000/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
21.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and Petitioner No.2 is son of deceased Prakash and he lost father's love and care and Petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased Prakash and she has lost the love and care of her son in her old age.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:

Smt.Lakshmamma vs Danappa on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186881783/
7 22.
The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
23. It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was taken at Rs.14,500/ p.m.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "
 Held :  yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40

sentences.text: Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation -
Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held:

Yes:
there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork : executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 25% between the age of 40 to 50 years".

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 48 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 25% of the income has to be added.
So, 25% of Rs.14,500/ comes to Rs.3,625/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.18,125/ p.m. (Rs.14,500/ + Rs. 3,625/).

8
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 13.

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.18,125/ it comes to Rs.12,083/ (
18,125/  6,042/) and multiplier applied is 13 which comes to Rs.18,84,948/ (12,083/ x 12 =
1,44,996/, Rs.1,44,996/ x 13 = 18,84,948/). Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,84,948/ towards loss of dependency.
COMPENSATION
TOWARDS
MEDICAL EXPENCES

The Petitioner No.1 has deposed that she has spent more than Rs.20,00,000/
towards medical expenses during the treatment period of deceased Prakash.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced 114 medical bills which totally marked at Ex.P.9.
I have gone through the medical bills and acceptable medical bills comes at Rs.13,63,436.50/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.13,63,500/ as a compensation under this head.

29. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
4.

Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.

Loss of Dependency Rs.18,84,948/
7.
Medical Expenses Rs.13,63,500/ Total Rs.33,73,448/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.33,73,448/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

30. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA51C1286.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid from 10.11.2019 to 09.11.2020 which is in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.

Though the Respondent No.2 taken contention that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle did not Smt.Lakshmamma vs Danappa on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186881783/
9 possess valid and effective Driving licence

sentences.text: , it has not produced the Driving licence of the driver to show that the same is not valid at the time of the accident.
In the cross examination of RW.1, he admitted that they did separate investigation from their company and obtained all the police documents and Driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, in the Charge sheet, I.O has not mentioned the offence u/s 3(1)r/w 181 of IMV Act against the driver of the offending vehicle for not possessing the Driving licence at the time of accident.
Moreover, RW.1 admitted in the cross examination that they have not challenged the charge sheet.
Therefore, Respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
31. Issue No.4 :
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.33,73,448/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.33,73,448/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

However, Respondent No.3 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 70% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 15% each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.3, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
